summary: First integration test iteration for Itinera app. Created pytest backend suite (17 tests) and Playwright UI flow. Backend: 16/17 passed — only brute-force lockout test failed because Kubernetes ingress rotates client source IPs, so the `ip:email` counter never reaches 5 for any single IP (a real security bug, not a test bug). Frontend: all critical flows pass (landing, signup → dashboard, create itinerary, 5 tabs, add event/expense/packing + toggle, map, edit, logout, protected-route redirect).

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout uses request.client.host which returns the immediate peer (k8s ingress/LB), and this IP rotates across a pool. 5 wrong attempts for the same email were distributed across multiple IPs, so no single `ip:email` bucket hit BRUTE_LIMIT — the 6th attempt returned 401 instead of 429. An attacker behind any proxy/IP pool can bypass lockout. Use X-Forwarded-For (with a trusted-proxy whitelist) or lock by email only (with a separate lower-threshold per-IP counter).

minor.issue: locked_until is written as a tz-aware datetime but MongoDB returns naive datetimes by default (motor tz_aware=False). Comparison `locked_until > now` (tz-aware) will raise TypeError if the threshold is ever reached — reachable only if the IP issue above is fixed. Use datetime.utcnow() + replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) on read, or configure motor with tz_aware=True.
Requires authentication (Depends(get_current_user)). If access token expired, user cannot logout to clear refresh cookie. Consider allowing unauthenticated logout that just clears cookies.

issues: Recharts warning: 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0'. The pie chart's ResponsiveContainer has no explicit min height; chart may fail to render on first mount. Wrap in a parent with fixed height (e.g. h-64) or add aspect/minHeight props.

action_items: Fix brute-force identifier: read client IP from X-Forwarded-For (first-hop with trusted proxies) or drop IP from the lockout key; additionally add an email-only counter with a higher threshold. Without this fix, brute-force protection is not effective behind the current ingress.
Handle naive datetimes from MongoDB when comparing `locked_until > now` (coerce to UTC-aware on read).
Give Budget pie chart ResponsiveContainer an explicit height (e.g. h-64) to silence recharts 0-dimension warning and ensure reliable render.
Consider allowing POST /api/auth/logout without auth (always clears cookies) so expired sessions can still log out cleanly.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py uses `@app.on_event('startup')` and `on_event('shutdown')` which are deprecated in modern FastAPI; prefer the lifespan context manager.

CORS middleware is added AFTER `app.include_router(api)`. In Starlette this still works (middlewares wrap the app at request time), but convention is to add middleware before mounting routers to keep ordering explicit.

Admin seed uses os.environ.get('ADMIN_EMAIL', 'admin@example.com') default but backend/.env sets admin@itinera.app — OK, but dropping the fallback would make missing config fail fast as required by env policy.
`logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` is declared but never used; dead code.

ItineraryUpdate filters out any field whose value is None, so callers cannot clear optional fields (e.g. set description back to empty). Only `exclude_unset=True` should be used; drop the `if v is not None` filter.
No pagination on GET /api/itineraries (limit 500). Acceptable for MVP; document for later.

Frontend: PDF export uses html2canvas on a fixed 780px off-screen node — OK, but `imgHeight` looping math may overlap content between pages when content is long. Consider slicing the canvas per page for exact pagination.
test_credentials: Admin admin@itinera.app / admin123 (working). Test users registered dynamically per run with unique emails to avoid 409.
seed_data_creation: Each pytest/UI run creates and cleans up TEST_-prefixed itineraries. Admin user seeded on backend startup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covers health, auth (register/login/me/logout/refresh/bad-pw/brute-force), and itinerary CRUD incl. cross-user isolation. The brute-force test will remain failing until the main agent fixes the lockout-key strategy to work behind the k8s ingress (use X-Forwarded-For or drop IP from key). Playwright UI flow covered: signup→dashboard→create→detail tabs (overview/timeline/map/budget/packing)→edit→logout→protected-route. PDF download was not triggered in the browser (would require file-download interception) but the button wiring and code path were code-reviewed.
rca_of_the_issue: RCA for failing brute-force test: On each HTTP request the FastAPI app reads `request.client.host` which — in this deployment — is the peer IP of the kube ingress/LB connection, and that IP changes across requests (observed identifiers `10.64.130.10:brute+…` and `10.64.128.135:brute+…` with count=3 each for the same email). Because the lockout bucket is keyed `ip:email`, 5 attempts to the same email split across multiple ingress IPs and no bucket hits BRUTE_LIMIT=5. Reproduction: register a user; send 5 wrong-password logins from the public URL; 6th attempt still returns 401. Mitigation: (a) parse `request.headers.get('X-Forwarded-For')` and take the left-most client IP with a trusted-proxy whitelist, or (b) remove IP from the key (lock by email only) with a slightly higher threshold + captcha on repeated failures, or (c) add a secondary per-IP counter in addition to per-email.
